subject: Exec handoff & renewal trajectory for BrightLane
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia@brightlane.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & capacity — BrightLane discussion

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Quick note to kick off our renewal planning — our term with Redwood is up in Q4 and we anticipate a ~1.6x throughput increase next year as we move more inference to real-time. Procurement asked that we get an initial timeline, a short list of stakeholders, and a tentative QBR window so they can align internal approvals.

High level:
- Current term ends: 2027-12-15
- Expected uplift: +60% monthly tokens (primarily chat embeddings & reranking)
- Interested in exploring 24-month term vs an annual renewal with staircase commits

Can you suggest a 2–3 week window for an exec handoff + QBR so we can line up our CTO (Brian) and procurement? Also please send any SOW/redline we should expect.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Infrastructure | BrightLane

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-20T11:03:00-07:00

On Sun, Sep 19, 2027 at 9:15 AM Alicia Torres <alicia@brightlane.com> wrote:
> Quick note to kick off our renewal planning — our term with Redwood is up in Q4 and we anticipate a ~1.6x throughput increase next year...

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and the usage file. High level proposal from our side:

1) Timeline & cadence
- Exec handoff and QBR (90 min): target week of Oct 4; alternate week of Oct 11.
- Internal procurement/contract work: we suggest running legal + procurement in parallel once SOW is agreed; target signature by 2027-11-15 to allow time for onboarding.

2) Term options
- 24-month committed term (preferred) with a 10% unit discount and predictable throughput lanes
- 12-month term with staircase commits (we'll structure burst buffers for seasonal variance)

3) Capacity & cost levers
- Recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for high-reuse chat flows (expected to reduce token spend by ~12%)
- Offer a performance-optimized quantization profile for batch reranking to reduce GPU hours for embeddings-heavy workloads

4) Stakeholders we should include on the QBR
- BrightLane: Alicia (infrastructure), Brian (CTO), Procurement (legal lead)
- Redwood: Karhtik (Account Exec), Laura (Solutions), Monica (Renewals lead), Hannah (Customer Success for onboarding)

Next steps: I'll attach an updated SOW draft and a short mutual action plan template. Can you confirm availability for Oct 4 vs Oct 11 (mornings PDT preferred) and whether Brian wants a 30-minute pre-brief?

Attachments:
- Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf
- mutual_action_plan_brightlane.xlsx

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful.

Brian is available for Oct 4 (10:00–11:30 PDT) for the QBR and would like a 30-minute technical pre-brief the day before (Oct 3) with your solutions engineer. Procurement copied here — procurement@brightlane.com will need the SOW redline and a billing cadence note for their vendor intake.

A few asks from our side:
- Can the SOW clearly call out data residency for EU customers we serve (we host a subset of BrightLane data in EU regions)?
- We need a clear rollback/fallback policy in the runbook for any observed latency regressions post-rollout.

I'll loop procurement on the DocuSign once we have a final SOW.
